title: Emission chain appends its remaining bits
statement: Let $c,C,q\in\mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be a bit string, let $h:\{0,\ldots,c\}\to\mathbb{Z}$ be a head-position function, and let $j\le C$ and $o$ be an output word. After exactly $j+1$ steps of the unary box-enumeration machine from the configuration on input $x$ in state $\mathrm{emit}_j$, with tape contents $1^q$ and head positions $h$, the machine is in state $\mathrm{advance}_0$, with the same tape contents and head positions, and output $o$ followed by $j$ copies of $1$.
hypotheses_covered: $h$ assigns integer head positions to indices $0,\ldots,c$
replaced: Let $c, C, q \in \mathbb{N}$, $x$ a bit string and $h \colon \{0,\dots,c\} \to \mathbb{Z}$. For every $j \le C$ and every output word $o$, running $\mathcal{P}_{c,C}$ for exactly $j+1$ steps from $\Gamma_q(\mathrm{emit}_j, h, o)$ yields $\Gamma_q(\mathrm{advance}_0, h, o\,1^j)$; here $\mathcal{P}_{c,C}$ is the unary box-enumeration machine with $c+1$ work tapes, which writes $1^{|x|+1}$ on every work tape and then runs $c+1$ nested unary loops, emitting $C$ ones per innermost iteration, and $\mathrm{loop}_i$, $\mathrm{rewind}_i$, $\mathrm{advance}_i$, $\mathrm{emit}_j$ are its control states, and $\Gamma_q(s,h,o)$ denotes its configuration on input $x$ in control state $s$, with the input head on the blank cell right of the input, every work tape holding $1^q$ in cells $0,\dots,q-1$ and blanks elsewhere, work head $k$ at position $h(k)$, and output $o$.
